clue.text: Strongly-made vehicle covered in rust

indicators.note: covered in says the vehicle is wrapped inside the word for rust

parts.note: rust is a form of decay, as rot is
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An old car built tough but now coated in corrosion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' puts BUS inside ROT, with rust taken as a kind of rot or decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something sturdy and solidly built is strongly made.

clue.text: School subject's precise limit

parts.note: RE (religious education) is a school subject
precise means strict, as in strict accuracy

explanation.surface: A school rule says exactly how far a subject may go.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, Religious Education, is a standard British school subject; the 's stands for 'is', joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to confine or set bounds on, a verb synonym of limit.

clue.text: Created favourable publicity for such an urban area

explanation.surface: A town gets good press for being heavily developed.
explanation.definitionFit: To build someone up is to praise them; a densely developed town district is described as built up.

clue.text: It may break the career of elevated artistes

definitions.text: It may break the career of elevated artistes

parts.words: It may break the career of elevated artistes
parts.note: break means cushion a fall, and career means a headlong rush downward, for acrobats high on the trapeze

explanation.surface: Something that could ruin the careers of famous performers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' seems to mean ruin and 'career' a job, but the thing breaks the plunge (career) of trapeze artistes who fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A mesh strung below high-wire acts catches falling performers.

clue.text: Unreliable and only half as visible as Big Ben?

definitions.text: only half as visible as Big Ben?

explanation.surface: A dubious claim that the clock tower shows only half its faces.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Ben's clock tower in London has four clock faces, so half of it shows two.
explanation.definitionFit: A deceitful, insincere person is two-faced; half of a four-dialled tower has just two dials.

clue.text: Diligent astronomer's motto? There's more

explanation.surface: A sky-watcher's slogan, promising further discoveries to come.
explanation.definitionFit: A careful stargazer keeps eyes on the heavens; the stock phrase promises further news soon.

clue.text: Fellow'sopposed to thiefbeing booked

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
agin is a dialect word meaning against or opposed to

explanation.surface: A man resisting a crook who is being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue runs words together ('Fellow's opposed to thief being booked'). 'booked' means appearing in a book: the thief is the one in Dickens's Oliver Twist, not one under arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: The leader of the pickpocket gang in Dickens's novel Oliver Twist is a literary criminal.

clue.text: In blue party, margins appear to be reddish

indicators.note: In says the margins go inside the party

parts.note: the Conservatives, whose colour is blue, are CON
rims are edges or margins

explanation.surface: A political report: Tory margins look like they're turning red.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, abbreviated CON.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep red shade is a colour in the red family.

clue.text: Spell out three consecutive letters in English

parts.note: D, E and F follow one another in the alphabet

explanation.surface: Writing a sequence of three letters in English.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell out a meaning is to explain it precisely.

clue.text: Excellent position for quickest delivery

explanation.surface: Top-ranking mail service for speedy despatch.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain first-class post is the faster, dearer tier of letter delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A first-class post is a top job; in UK mail it is the premium, next-day service.

clue.text: Pelt with stone one that's near

parts.note: a pelt is an animal's skin
flint is a hard stone

explanation.surface: Someone throws rocks at a person standing close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pelt' looks like a verb (throw at), but it is a noun. 'near' is old slang for mean or stingy, not close by.
explanation.definitionFit: Near in the sense of tight-fisted describes a miser.

clue.text: Sorrow as good fire goes out

indicators.note: goes out suggests the fire is disrupted, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Sadness as a cosy fire dies down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes out' rearranges FIRE into RIEF after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep sadness, such as mourning, is synonymous with sorrow.

clue.text: Turns round to stare excitedly

indicators.note: excitedly says the letters of to stare are agitated into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spins about to gawp in excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolve or spin is to turn round.

clue.text: Bequeaths such practical experience

explanation.surface: A will passes on real, practical know-how.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass along to an heir is to bequeath; direct practical involvement is described as hands-on.

clue.text: Meat dish gangster can't finish

indicators.note: can't finish says the gangster's surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster fails to clear his plate of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated, fattened cockerel is served as a meat course.

clue.text: Criminal and assistant finally brought round to this place for hanging together

indicators.note: brought round to says these pieces wrap around the words for this place

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
here means this place

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of assistant

explanation.surface: A felon and his accomplice are led to the gallows here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought round to' puts HERE inside CONT, the convict plus the T ending 'assistant'. 'hanging' suggests execution but means sticking together.
explanation.definitionFit: Logical, consistent arguments hold together, as parts that cohere.

clue.text: As after-dinner speaker, curate runs on dreadfully

indicators.note: dreadfully says the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A clergyman giving a speech at a dinner drones on far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' shuffles CURATE, R and ON together.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled teller of anecdotes, the kind hired to entertain at banquets.

clue.text: Sadly, a bit up the pole

explanation.surface: Feeling down, and slightly crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up the pole' is British slang for mad, but here it is a literal flagpole.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags flown partway down signal mourning, a sad occasion; the position is literally some way up the flagpole.

clue.text: Marriage condemned in St Paul

indicators.note: condemned suggests the letters are wrecked and rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: A wedding at St Paul's Cathedral is denounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding ceremony, the rite of matrimony.

clue.text: Head off unspoken anger and offence

indicators.note: Head off says the word for unspoken loses its first letter

parts.note: dumb means silent, unspoken
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Stopping silent fury before it turns to insult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' removes the D from DUMB to leave UMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking umbrage means taking offence, feeling resentment.

clue.text: Snake or swan depicted by artist

parts.note: a cob is a male swan
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter chooses between a serpent and a swan as subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A venomous hooded serpent of Asia and Africa.

clue.text: Sensitive fellow-citizen let off

parts.note: a Brit is a fellow citizen to a British reader

indicators.note: off says the letters of let are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: A delicate compatriot is excused.
explanation.definitionFit: Easily shattered or fragile, as a touchy temperament is.

clue.text: Fuss and bother is healthy around ship

indicators.note: around says the word for healthy encloses the ship

parts.note: hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Fit and well, someone is still bothered by a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying trouble or bother, a nuisance.

clue.text: Shrub by a river, only American

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child
US is the United States, American

explanation.surface: A bush by a river is found only in America.
explanation.definitionFit: The strawberry tree is an evergreen plant of this genus.

clue.text: Partially cut a long nail

indicators.note: Partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fingernail trimmed only part of the way.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird of prey's claw, a hooked nail.

clue.text: Religious leader quiet about disagreement

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music
on means about, concerning
a tiff is a minor quarrel

explanation.surface: A churchman stays silent over a dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope, as Supreme Pontiff, is a chief priest.

clue.text: Obstruct monk's seat

explanation.surface: Blocking a friar from his chair.
explanation.definitionFit: To stall is to delay or hinder; a stall is a fixed seat in a church choir.

clue.text: Their leader's always on the fiddle

definitions.text: Their leader's always on the fiddle

parts.words: Their leader's always on the fiddle
parts.note: on the fiddle suggests a cheat, but the leader of this group is the principal violinist

explanation.surface: A gang whose boss is a perpetual swindler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' is British slang for cheating; here it literally means playing the violin, as the leader (first violinist) does.
explanation.definitionFit: A symphonic ensemble is led by its first violin.

clue.text: Period apprehensible in entirety? Yes and no

indicators.note: apprehensible in says the letters can be found within the word entirety
Yes and no says the letters are there but not in the right order

explanation.surface: Can a span of time ever be grasped entirely? Partly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters are all in 'entirety' (yes) but jumbled (no), so it is an anagram signalled by 'apprehensible in' and 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless time, a period without end.

clue.text: Colourful painting detains officer briefly

indicators.note: detains says the painting holds the officer inside it

parts.note: art is painting
GEN is the short form of general, an officer

explanation.surface: A vivid canvas holds a general captive for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: Argent is the heraldic tincture silver, so it counts as a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, silver is one of the tinctures used on coats of arms.
